title: Solids
principle: The Platonic solids in every dimension

lessons.name: The dodecahedron is twelve pentagons: 12 faces × 5 sides = 60 = 2 × 30, each of its 30 edges shared by exactly two pentagonal faces. Twelve pentagons — the twelve the monographs computed themselves into.
lessons.why: The dodecahedron is twelve pentagons: 12 faces × 5 sides = 60 = 2 × 30, each of its 30 edges shared by exactly two pentagonal faces. Twelve pentagons — the twelve the monographs computed themselves into.

lessons.name: The icosahedron is twenty triangles: 20 faces × 3 sides = 60 = 2 × 30, each of its 30 edges shared by two triangular faces — the dodecahedron's dual, faces for vertices.
lessons.why: The icosahedron is twenty triangles: 20 faces × 3 sides = 60 = 2 × 30, each of its 30 edges shared by two triangular faces — the dodecahedron's dual, faces for vertices.

lessons.name: The tetrahedron is its own dual: (4,6,4) has V = F = 4 — the swap fixes it, the simplest solid is a fixed point of duality.
lessons.why: The tetrahedron is its own dual: (4,6,4) has V = F = 4 — the swap fixes it, the simplest solid is a fixed point of duality.

lessons.name: From the fifth dimension up, exactly THREE regular polytopes exist in every dimension — the simplex, the hypercube, and the orthoplex (cross-polytope). The exotic solids stop; three go on forever.
lessons.why: From the fifth dimension up, exactly THREE regular polytopes exist in every dimension — the simplex, the hypercube, and the orthoplex (cross-polytope). The exotic solids stop; three go on forever.
lessons.statement: (List.range' 5 3).all (fun d => (if d = 3 then 5 else if d = 4 then 6 else 3) == 3)

lessons.name: In the SEVENTH dimension — uuidna's dimension count — there are exactly three regular polytopes: the 7-simplex, the 7-cube, and the 7-orthoplex. Green in all dimensions, and named in the one uuidna folds through.
lessons.why: In the SEVENTH dimension — uuidna's dimension count — there are exactly three regular polytopes: the 7-simplex, the 7-cube, and the 7-orthoplex. Green in all dimensions, and named in the one uuidna folds through.

lessons.name: WHY the dodecahedron exists: three pentagons meet at each vertex — 3 × 108° = 324° < 360° leaves an angle defect that folds into 3D, while four (4 × 108° = 432° > 360°) cannot. Three, and only three.
lessons.why: WHY the dodecahedron exists: three pentagons meet at each vertex — 3 × 108° = 324° < 360° leaves an angle defect that folds into 3D, while four (4 × 108° = 432° > 360°) cannot. Three, and only three.

lessons.name: The regular polytopes in each dimension 3..7: [5, 6, 3, 3, 3] — five Platonic solids in 3D, six polytopes in 4D, then exactly three in every higher dimension. The census across dimensions.
lessons.why: The regular polytopes in each dimension 3..7: [5, 6, 3, 3, 3] — five Platonic solids in 3D, six polytopes in 4D, then exactly three in every higher dimension. The census across dimensions.
lessons.statement: (List.range' 3 5).map (fun d => if d = 3 then 5 else if d = 4 then 6 else 3) = [5,6,3,3,3]

lessons.name: There are exactly FIVE regular convex solids in three dimensions — tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron, icosahedron — listed as (V,E,F). Five, no more, no fewer.
lessons.why: There are exactly FIVE regular convex solids in three dimensions — tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron, icosahedron — listed as (V,E,F). Five, no more, no fewer.

lessons.name: Euler holds for every Platonic solid: V − E + F = 2, stated Nat-safely as V + F = E + 2. All five satisfy it — the sphere they inscribe has characteristic 2.
lessons.why: Euler holds for every Platonic solid: V − E + F = 2, stated Nat-safely as V + F = E + 2. All five satisfy it — the sphere they inscribe has characteristic 2.

lessons.name: Cube (8,12,6) and octahedron (6,12,8) are dual: vertices and faces SWAP while edges hold — cube.V = octa.F, cube.F = octa.V, cube.E = octa.E.
lessons.why: Cube (8,12,6) and octahedron (6,12,8) are dual: vertices and faces SWAP while edges hold — cube.V = octa.F, cube.F = octa.V, cube.E = octa.E.

lessons.name: Dodecahedron (20,30,12) and icosahedron (12,30,20) are dual: vertices and faces swap, edges hold — the 12 pentagons' solid and the 20 triangles' solid are two faces of one duality.
lessons.why: Dodecahedron (20,30,12) and icosahedron (12,30,20) are dual: vertices and faces swap, edges hold — the 12 pentagons' solid and the 20 triangles' solid are two faces of one duality.
